hypothesis: Is the fully closed prior-minute BTC-USD return incrementally predictive of the next ETH-USD M1 return versus ETH own lagged return under realistic transaction costs?

prior_art.scope_note: Binance, 30 cryptocurrencies; positive evidence for cross-crypto lag, not proof of profitable Coinbase BTC/ETH M1 replication
prior_art.title: Cross-cryptocurrency return predictability

prior_art.scope_note: Hourly/daily BTC-ETH price leadership mixed and economic exploitability limited
prior_art.title: Lead-Lag relationship between Bitcoin and Ethereum: Evidence from hourly and daily data

prior_art.scope_note: Larger altcoins including ETH show mainly contemporaneous rather than lagged responses at minute frequency
prior_art.title: Price Transmission from Bitcoin to Altcoins: High-Frequency Evidence and Implications for Trading Strategy

proposed_data.source: Coinbase Exchange public spot M1 OHLC

controls: Prior completed ETH M1 log return
proposed_prediction_contract.execution_sequencing: Any later trade signal at close of fully observed source bar; prospective simulated entry no earlier than next ETH M1 opening, fees and slippage required
proposed_prediction_contract.information_set: Only BTC and ETH bars already fully closed at decision time; never current unfinished BTC candle
proposed_prediction_contract.missingness: Reject missing, stale, duplicated or misaligned minute pairs, exclude windows across any gap
proposed_prediction_contract.predictor: Prior completed BTC M1 log return
proposed_prediction_contract.risk: No claims of executable best bid/ask from OHLC; evaluate fees/spread/slippage conservatively or reject if unevidenced
proposed_prediction_contract.selection: No parameter search, no choosing best lag after seeing results; compare the single fixed lag against controls
proposed_prediction_contract.target: Subsequent completed ETH M1 log return strictly after predictor becomes known
